CHIEF COMPLAINT
Yearly exam.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Beverly is a 24-year-old female with a history of type 2 diabetes and hypertension presenting for her yearly exam. She reports that she has been doing well overall. She recently started working in a bakery this summer and has been enjoying it, but notes that she has been snacking a lot during shifts and eating significantly more desserts than usual. She reports her blood sugars have been up and down, which she attributes to her diet. She confirms she has been taking her medication as prescribed and has not missed any doses. She notes that her blood pressure has been good despite the fluctuating diabetes levels. She is sleeping well, getting a full eight hours of sleep. She denies any concerns about hurting herself.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Nurse performed a review of systems. Patient reports no additional concerns beyond what has been discussed.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Type 2 diabetes
Hypertension
Grade 2 systolic ejection murmur (unchanged)

MEDICATIONS
Metformin twice daily
Lisinopril 10 mg once daily

ALLERGIES
Not discussed.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not discussed.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Recently started working in a bakery this summer. Reports difficulty resisting temptation from desserts at work.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm with grade 2 systolic ejection murmur, unchanged from prior exams. Lungs: Clear. Grips: Equal bilaterally. Neurovascular: Intact. Carotid bruits: None. Thyromegaly: None. Edema: None. Pulses: Good. Neurological: Able to feel touch. Overall exam essentially normal.

RESULTS
Hemoglobin A1c: Elevated
Blood pressure: Good/normal
Vital signs: Good

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Diabetes: Hemoglobin A1c is elevated, indicating blood sugars have been out of control. Goal hemoglobin A1c under 7, preferably under 6. Not changing current metformin medication at this time as this appears diet-related. Patient instructed to cut down on snacking and additional sweets. Patient to check blood sugars in the morning and call in fasting blood sugar in about two weeks. Follow-up appointment in about two months to reassess. If hemoglobin A1c has not improved, will discuss adding another medication.

Hypertension: Relatively stable on current regimen. Continue lisinopril 10 mg once daily. No changes at this time.
